source: And... as you are the man closest to him, I must ask you what you know of any threats to the crown.
Help with what, my lord?
Ophelia told me you requested my presence. Didn't you?
I'm afraid not. Although, now that I have you here...
I heard a rumor as well, one which I'd like to expunge or confirm rather quickly.
Lord Polonius, you've always been closest to the crown. Do you know of anyone who might threaten the safety of our court?
I'm afraid I know precious little. I'm by His Majesty's side all day.
And what of the times when you aren't by His Majesty's side?
I'll be curt, Lord Polonius. We have it on good word that you were spotted discarding documents in private.
Was King Claudius ever privy to these documents? And if not, what cause would you have to hide them?
I cannot say. My word prevents me.
You must understand how this appears, my lord. You, the King's most trusted advisor, withholding this during wartime...
I'm no spy, Bernardo.
Then prove it. Tell me what was in those documents.
Ah! In my few spare personal hours, I am often locked in my room. I've a right to my privacy!
Rest assured that I've given His Majesty my weight in loyalty thrice over. As I did to his brother before him.
To whom would you be more loyal, had you the choice?
W-well, that's not entirely a fair question. Were His Majesty Hamlet still alive, King Claudius would be but a King in waiting.
Pardon my forwardness, Lord Polonius. You're right, of course.
You're free to leave.
Thank you, Guard Captain.
You've brought this upon yourself, then. Whatever the King decides.
Were I you, I'd prepare to make a statement before His Majesty—one which is better than what you just told me.
(Oh, God, what will become of me?)
Best wishes, Lord Polonius.
Lord Polonius.
My final request. Show me those documents.
Look upon the hearth. You'll see the remains of them there.
Then I'm here to place you under arrest, my lord.
Of course you are. As I knew you would be.
Please come with me. I expect I won't have to have my men take you to your cell in chains.
Come, now, Bernardo. We're both gentlemen here. I find even the query offensive. I'll go gladly.
Ophelia, I apologize. You needn't be here for this, if you don't want to.
Of course I'll go too.
(Father... he's putting on such a face. He's terrified.)
Well, then.
I trusted you. My brother trusted you. How can it have come to this?
It is precisely because of the trust your brother and I had for one another that we are standing here now.
Hmph. Pretty words, but treason is treason. You've been smuggling information about our comings and goings to our enemies.
And for that reason, you shall stay here as long as you live.
Even despite your station, house arrest is too kind for a treasoner.
...Very well, my lord.
Here I shall remain.
Father, this is insane. Just show them the notes. I know you're not a spy!
Why must you be so stubborn?
My love, for your own sake, you'd better not speak to me again.
Go. Please. Go and leave me in peace.
(Oh, Father...)
(He'll do anything to protect King Hamlet's legacy—but even now, he's going too far.)
(What could possibly be in those notes? I have to find out.)
It isn't possible you can really be dead, is it?
You absolute sniveling fool. How dare you leave us like this. And in such a trivial, horrible way.
What on earth are the people who love you going to do now, Hamlet?
What in hell am I going to do now?
I followed you everywhere. Across the entire world and back. Through all these years...
And finally you go somewhere I can't follow you. How is that fair?
I never worked up the courage to say it. I'm a bloody fool.
Even now, it's hard to say it...
Well, then. Well then, Hamlet.
I loved you, you bloody idiot. I will always love you.
It feels sometimes like I've been through several men's lifetimes. Like I should have died on your father's battlefield, or at sea, or of plague.
But I always felt I was meant to live for something more. And then I only wanted to live for you.
Your stupid cocky smile. Your easily-suffering heart. I've loved a lot of men, but none like you.
Your lack of any and all sense of humor. Damn you. I loved it all, and I wanted you all for myself, body and soul.
But I, like all the others, realized it was useless to try and have you.
Always did hunger for the unreachable things in life.
At least I got to speak with you about it. Just once. I had hoped for that, I think. This closure.
Now... I have to go on, somehow. I have to... rebuild.
And I don't want to. I'd rather give up and die right here. It'd be easy.
But I'm not going to, Hamlet.
I'm going to live. I can never know for sure, but I think you would've wanted me to live.
And someday, maybe I can find some other dark-haired man to follow to the ends of the earth.
He'll never be you. But perhaps I can love him just the same.
Farewell, my friend. You were the best of them, even if you never believed it.
You would've wanted flights of angels to sing you to rest. For you, I can believe in a God that has you wrapped in His embrace.
Rest in peace. Now, and forevermore.
Do we have to talk to her, Rosie?
Of course we do. We are of noble blood. We pay our debts, no matter how unsavory they might be.
B-but I'm afraid of her!
Don't be silly. She's just one woman.
...Hello, Irma.
So if I turn you upside down and shake you, will all the money you owe me fall out?
Er-r-r... not quite. We are, as it were, in a particularly delicate position—
We're penniless!
Precisely. All those card games have drained what funds we brought to Elsinore.
(...And Irma's trick deck didn't do us any favors, either...)
As you've won more games than we have funds to pay, we are, in short, unable to pay you.
This is a wonderful position to be in.
It... is?
For me. Now I have two new servant girls to help me get my work done.
N-now hold on just a minute...
We're nobody's servants!
Do I need to extract my payment from you some other way? Rip those fine clothes off your bodies and sell them, perhaps?
What do you need us to do...?
Oh, a bit here, a bit there.
First, I want you both to collect some moss from that old fountain in the courtyard.
Gives all of my soups a nice, earthy flavor. Don't ask.
After that... since you're both educated little birds, I need you to go to the gallery and find me something new to make for the Queen's birthday next month.
After that... since you're both educated little birds, I need you to go to the gallery and find me something new to make.
I can't read, so you'll have to remember it for me, then come tell it to me later.
And finally, I want you to gather the mushrooms that grow near the pond in the woods.
About ten dozen should be enough.
...What! All of that?
You can't be serious. We are women of noble families! Not your scullery maids!
And who do you think I am? My connections run far and wide, ladies. You know I have friends in powerful places.
Either get to work, or I'll take collateral from you in any way I see fit... By force, if needed.
Y-yes, ma'am...
...Then let's get to work.
It's in here.
How can you be sure...?
I don't want to reach my hand in there. This fountain probably hasn't been cleaned since Ogier the Dane was alive!
Well, I don't want to get my hands dirty, either.
We'll need to choose by some sort of objective, reasonable criteria.
For example: Age. I'm older, so I say you have to put your hand in the fountain.
Well, I can't argue with that logic.
I-it's so slimy!
And it's all over my hand...
Got some!
Do you think this much is enough?
(Is she... holding... moss?)
I can't see ever needing any more. Blech.
Let's go. Quickly, before anyone more sees us making uncomely idiots of ourselves.
There should be one particular tome here...
Do you see it?
Shh. Do you want people to see us?
Here it is. 'Das Buch von guter Speise.' The book of good food.
But where is it?
I don't know. I'll select something at random.
There's so much in here. And i-it's all in German!
Say, Rosie... I've never looked at these portraits up close.
Queen Astrid was... beautiful, wasn't she?
I heard from my father she passed away, but... why did she die?
Hamlet won't say. I think it was rather bloody.
I know she died a raving lunatic.
It's not the sort of thing one asks about in polite company. At least, not here.
Regardless, we've done the job we came here to do. Let us head to our next task anon.
Found some over here.
And more, here!
We look like idiots.
H-how many do we need to gather, again?
Ten dozen. We didn't bring anything to carry them in, so I'll have to use my skirts...
Guilda! Stop eating them!
But we've been working all day, and I'm hungry.
You're unbelievable.
Let's report our findings.
Your reign of tyrrany has come to an end, Irma. We've done everything on your list.
Such helpful lasses. I see you arranged everything I asked for. We'll have a stew of champions this eve.
Now begone. You're both horrid at cards and even worse at paying your gambling debts.
But as of this moment, we are settled, are we not?
You've added a single coin to the pile, but I intend to shake you for the rest at some later date.
From one 'friend' to another, I recommend you never deal in at my table again.
We never will!
(She's a cheat, anyhow...)
What was that?
N-nothing! We'll be going now!
This is a mere formality, Marcellus. Thank you for coming.
Wot's this all about now?
Have you witnessed any strange comings and goings lately? Anyone who might be a threat to the throne?
W-well... yeh know, I can't say I have.
Horatio asked me about a certain figure he saw leavin' Elsinore and headin' to town...
But I told him it could be all kinds o' people, and not to fret.
I think he's keepin' a vigilant watch, though.
That isn't his area of responsibility. I ought to have him removed from the watch rounds.
He's tardy enough as it is.
Erm... but, Captain... Suppose someone does attempt to track down this mysterious figure...?
Aren't yeh concerned what they might find?
I'm absurdly busy at the moment, Marcellus. I haven't time to worry about the one-man Italian Anti-Crime Brigade.
